# tiny-llm-router

> Zero-dependency model router for Python AI agents. Role-based picking, cost caps, latency guards, circuit-breakers. Single file, MIT.

- Version: 0.1.0
- License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/hussain-alsaibai/tiny-llm-router
- Language: Python (3.8+)
- Runtime dependencies: 0
- Install: `pip install tiny-llm-router` (or copy `tiny_llm_router.py`)
- Docs: README.md, `pyproject.toml`, `benchmark.py`, `test_tiny_llm_router.py`

## What this library does

Routes a `Task` (role, prompt metadata, image flag, latency budget) to one of N
LLM model names based on role rules, cost caps, observed latency, and a
circuit-breaker on flaky providers. Maintains rolling statistics and integrates
with `tiny-llm` via `make_tiny_llm_adapter(router, tiny_llm_module)`.

## When to use it

- You call 2+ LLM models and want consistent routing logic.
- You want cost caps per role (don't blow budget on chat, but allow o1 for think).
- You want auto-failover when a provider has N errors in T seconds.
- You want role-based cost attribution for agents (chat vs think vs vision).
- You want zero-dep, single-file library.

## When NOT to use it

- You only use one model.
- You need transformer-based learned routing (use Aviary / NotDiamond).
- You need LLM-side guardrails (use NeMo Guard / Llama Guard).

## Public API

- `Task(role, prompt, has_images, estimated_input_tokens, needs_json, latency_budget_ms, metadata)`
- `RoleRule(role, model, max_cost_per_1k, max_latency_p95_ms, only_if)`
- `Router(rules, fallback, pricing, failure_window_s, failure_threshold)`
- `router.pick(task) -> model_name` (raises `RoutingError`)
- `router.record(model, latency_ms, cost_usd, errored=False)` — update stats
- `router.stats(model=None) -> dict`
- `router.is_healthy(model) -> bool`
- `infer_role(task) -> str` — heuristic inference (code, vision, json, long, default)
- `make_tiny_llm_adapter(router, tiny_llm_module) -> Adapter` with `.chat_auto(task)`

## Code example

```python
from tiny_llm_router import Router, RoleRule, Task

router = Router([
    RoleRule("code",    "gpt-4o-mini", max_cost_per_1k=0.5),
    RoleRule("think",   "o1-mini"),
    RoleRule("vision",  "gpt-4o"),
    RoleRule("long",    "gemini-2.5-flash"),
    RoleRule("json",    "haiku"),
    RoleRule("default", "gpt-4o-mini"),
], fallback="haiku")

model = router.pick(Task(role="code", prompt="def fib(n): ..."))
# => "gpt-4o-mini"

# Auto-route via tiny-llm
import tiny_llm
adapter = make_tiny_llm_adapter(router, tiny_llm)
resp = adapter.chat_auto(Task(role="think", prompt="prove sqrt(2) irrational"))
```

## Integration with the tiny-* ecosystem

- Above `tiny-llm` — picks which model to dispatch to.
- Beside `tiny-cost` and `tiny-budget` — provides per-model cost attribution.
- Below `tiny-workflow-engine` — each step declares its own role.
- Inputs from `tiny-config` — load model/pricing tables from YAML.

## Compatibility

- Python 3.8 – 3.13 confirmed.
- No C extensions. No native deps.
- Thread-safe via single internal lock.

## Common pitfalls

1. `task.role` is optional; default `"default"` triggers heuristic inference.
2. Cost caps require a `pricing=` table on Router; otherwise cap is a no-op.
3. Circuit-breaker window is wall-clock; bursty traffic resets per `failure_window_s`.
4. Recorded stats persist in-process; restart loses them (intentional — no I/O).

## Changelog

- 0.1.0 — initial release: role rules, cost caps, latency guards, circuit-breakers,
  tiny-llm adapter, heuristic inference.
